reason: E1 supports the SCCP concept for strength-ductility synergy in a tungsten HEA at ambient and 800°C, but provides no evidence on thermal conductivity, carbide precipitates, or irradiation resistance. E2 evaluates thermal and irradiation resistance of different W-containing HEAs but does not involve coherent precipitates or the SCCP process. The key premises on thermal conduction, carbide formation, and performance under simultaneous heat flux and irradiation are unsupported by the cited evidence.
premises: Coherent nanoprecipitates can be induced in tungsten-based HEAs by a tailored heat-treatment (SCCP process).
Coherent interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, preserving ductility.
Coherent carbide precipitates provide efficient thermal conduction pathways.
The SCCP-processed alloy maintains high strength at elevated temperatures (up to 800°C, extendable to 1200°C).
The proposed alloy system is suitable for plasma-facing intermediate layers and resists irradiation-induced degradation.
